clue.text: Way to describe cold spell

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the word for way surrounds the cold letter

parts.note: a way can be a path
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A weather report: how to describe a run of chilly days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like part of the weather picture, a cold spell, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a short period of time, as in a bad stretch of form.

clue.text: Report about daughter in school given after time?

indicators.note: in places that unit inside the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: about means the report word goes round the daughter letter

parts.note: to state is to report

explanation.surface: A school report on a daughter that arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of sea creatures, not a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque bearing a later date than when it is handed over is dated after the time.

clue.text: Dish of recycled pasta

indicators.note: recycled means the letters of pasta are reused in a new order

explanation.surface: A meal made from leftover pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish small plates served as snacks are a dish.

clue.text: Bear's tail in rough shelter

indicators.note: tail in picks out the final letter of the word rough

parts.note: an arbour is a leafy shelter or bower in a garden

explanation.surface: A bear's tail caught in a rough shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the definition, a verb, with 's for is; it is not the animal whose tail is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a grudge is to hold or nurse it inwardly.

clue.text: Eating fruit, leaderless team with four supporters

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it
leaderless means the team word loses its first letter

parts.note: a squad is a team
a drupe is a stone fruit such as a plum or cherry

explanation.surface: A sports team with no captain munching fruit, propped up by four fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' suggests fans of the team, but here they are legs; 'leaderless' removes the opening letter of the team word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective meaning four-footed, an animal standing on four legs.

clue.text: Church edited out of sequence shot in part of New York

indicators.note: shot means ruined, so the remaining letters are rearranged
edited out of means the church letters are removed from sequence

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church scene cut from a film sequence shot in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing CE from SEQUENCE leaves SQUENE, which 'shot' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: A child celebrity turned up in concert

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the celebrity word is read upwards

parts.note: a name is a celebrity, as in a big name

explanation.surface: A child star made an appearance at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in concert' looks like the place the star appeared, but means together.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together, all united like a single person.

clue.text: Sting's flair for setting up bass

parts.note: to sting is to rob or swindle; the 's reads as is

indicators.note: setting up in a down clue means the flair word is read upwards

parts.note: a nose is a flair for something, as in a nose for news

explanation.surface: The singer Sting's knack for arranging bass lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' looks like the singer and bass player, but it is a verb meaning cheat. Paul Robeson was a famous American bass singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names his voice type: he was a celebrated deep-voiced singer.

clue.text: Bell public house about to enter a draw?

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for a public house

indicators.note: to enter means the about letter goes inside the draw

parts.note: one-all is a drawn score in football
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A pub called the Bell about to draw a raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like a pub name; it means a ring on the telephone, as in 'give me a bell'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang 'give me a bell' means ring me, so a bell is a ring on the telephone.

clue.text: Dean's party ruined NYE

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of NYE are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A dean's party spoiled New Year's Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean can be the senior member of a group, its most respected elder.

clue.text: Who's first to save a male in our comic?

definitions.text: Who's first to save a male in our comic?

indicators.note: first to picks out the opening letter of the word save
in places the preceding pieces inside the shuffled letters
comic means the letters of our are played around with

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A question about who rescues a man in a comic book story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' makes URO; 'a' means each, as in five pounds a head. The whole clue also describes the answer: the comic-book figure first to the rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: A caped comic-book champion is the one who rushes first to rescue anyone in danger.

clue.text: Happy young man touring Australia

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the young man's word encloses the country

parts.note: a boy is a young man
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A cheerful lad on a trip round Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is slang for slightly drunk, merry after a few drinks.

clue.text: Row about one's first of January ball results in split

indicators.note: about means the noise word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving IS

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of January

parts.note: a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A quarrel about someone's first New Year dance leads to a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it gives only its round shape, O.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or divide things that were joined is to split them.

clue.text: Report that is rejected about one type of drink

indicators.note: about means the turned pieces go round the single letter
rejected means sent back, so these joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: news is a report
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A news story that is dismissed concerning some drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NEWSIE into EISWEN; 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A German dessert wine made from grapes frozen on the vine is a type of drink.

clue.text: Month of British riots

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the words British riots

explanation.surface: A month of unrest on Britain's streets.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first month of the Jewish civil calendar, falling around September and October.

clue.text: Pottery in sink filled with extremely light veg

indicators.note: filled with means the sink word takes the light letters inside

parts.note: to sag is to sink

indicators.note: extremely takes the first and last letters of light

parts.note: to veg out is to laze

explanation.surface: Light vegetables piled into a sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veg' looks like vegetables but is the verb, to lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware glazed by throwing salt into the hot kiln is a kind of pottery.

clue.text: Canvas home — it's in the post

indicators.note: in puts the home and it pieces inside the post

parts.note: mail is the post
to be in is to be at home
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: A painting is sent home through the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails are made of canvas, so the principal sail of a ship can be called canvas.

clue.text: Allowed to admit chef's first to recycle cookware

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the allowed word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of chef's

parts.note: to reuse is to recycle

explanation.surface: A chef allowed to recycle kitchen pots.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a French brand of enamelled cast-iron pans and casseroles.

clue.text: One helped to see columns in the grid again and again and again, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a matching sound

parts.words: columns in the grid again and again and again
parts.note: the puzzle's number, 1111, is four ones, each like an upright column or the letter I; columns 2, 6, 10 and 14 of the grid spell ONE four times

explanation.surface: A cryptic puzzle about counting the columns in a grid over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue celebrates Toughie No. 1,111: four I-shaped columns spoken aloud sound like the insult for a spectacle wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking nickname for someone who wears glasses, someone helped to see by lenses.

clue.text: Spilt oil and it spread

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters of oil and it are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some oil was spilt and it spread across the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Widening or expansion, as of the pupils, is a spread in size.

clue.text: Nonsense that will primarily confuse

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letters of that and will

parts.note: to addle is to confuse

explanation.surface: A complaint that some nonsense will mainly cause confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly talk or rubbish is nonsense.

clue.text: Inclined to emphasise everything inside facility is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the remaining letters are put in a different order
everything inside takes all the letters of facility but its two ends

explanation.surface: A complaint that everything in some building is faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is used to give a word stress on the page.

clue.text: Filipino's term to describe lady love

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the language belonging to Filipinos

indicators.note: to describe is to draw round, so the term word encloses the others

parts.note: a tag is a label or term
gal is an informal word for a lady
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Filipino's word for his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the main native language of the Philippines, the tongue that belongs to Filipinos.

clue.text: A gesture oddly easy for those taking charge

parts.note: a nod is a gesture of the head

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of easy

explanation.surface: An easy gesture for people taking command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking charge' looks like leadership, but it is electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrodes are where electrical current, or charge, enters a device.

clue.text: Clipped sound — song in 80s style

indicators.note: clipped means the sea inlet word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bight is a bay or inlet, like a sound
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A trimmed noise and a tune in an eighties manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' is a body of water here, not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Large backcombed, heavily sprayed hairdos were a signature look of the 1980s.

clue.text: Retard's run through fire

indicators.note: through means the run letter goes right inside the fire word

parts.note: to fire pottery is to bake it in a kiln
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Something holding back a run through flames.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard is to slow down, as a car's stopping device does.

clue.text: Close game, one put on after dark

parts.note: nigh means close or near
a tie is a match in a knockout competition, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A tight match where one player comes on late in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment put on at bedtime.

clue.text: Latin subject put together by the educated person

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A Latin topic set by a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a topic or theme, used in English for a subject of discourse.

clue.text: Give a pencil back

indicators.note: back means the drawing word is read in reverse

parts.note: to pencil is to draw

explanation.surface: A request to hand a pencil back.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant or bestow something, such as a prize, is to give it.

clue.text: They make peak calls so elderly will suffer

indicators.note: will suffer suggests the letters of so elderly are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that older folk will feel the strain of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers warble their calls from mountain peaks.

clue.text: Square found in other square snack

indicators.note: found in puts the first square word inside the other word

parts.note: else means other, as in someone else
to be square is to be even, owing nothing
S is an abbreviation for square, as in street names

explanation.surface: A square sitting inside another square, like a puzzle grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'square's do different jobs: EVEN for quits, S as its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A light mid-morning bite, taken about eleven o'clock, is a snack.

clue.text: Core of progress behind hard work

indicators.note: core of takes the middle letters of the word progress

parts.note: aft means behind, towards the stern of a ship

explanation.surface: Progress lagging behind despite toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is British slang for strenuous effort, toil.
